pitch_detail.notes: Head north from the gap, side-hilling on the left, then cut back across under Glacier Gap Peak (7,739 ft on some maps) and climb onto the ridge again. Stay on the ridge to roughly 8,400 ft; the ground is easy snow and ridge walking.

Near 8,400 ft leave the ridge and traverse northeast onto the upper Suiattle Glacier, keeping below and east of a band of cliffs, until the upper Cool Glacier is reached at about 9,200 ft. Disappointment Peak drops big rocks, so give its flank a wide berth.

Climb the Cool Glacier westward, rounding the west side of Disappointment Peak, and regain the ridge at the glacier's top. Crevasses widen as summer advances. Beyond, a pumice ridge leads north, finishing on a short, steep snow slope in early season.

review.changed: Wrote all three boxes from two pages that agree on the line; no lengths or anchors stated. Kept stored NE traverse, rockfall and ridge-regain facts. Several other pages (Mountaineers reports, SummitPost, CascadeClimbers) refused or would not load.
review.other_findings: The stored beta describes a Disappointment Peak variant over class 3-4 ground; the Mountain Project page describes it as a South Ridge alternative to Disappointment Peak with loose rock. The route name says 'Disappointment Peak Cleaver' but the stored line is Gerdine/Cool; those are related but distinct routes.
